title: Treatments for Varicose Veins/Venous Insufficiency

criteria.question: Does imaging (typically duplex ultrasound) demonstrate reflux in the great or small saphenous vein?
criteria.evidence_hint: Duplex/venous ultrasound report: reflux, incompetence, reflux duration, GSV/SSV/SFJ/SPJ.

criteria.question: Is the documented CEAP clinical class C2 or higher (varicose veins or worse: edema, skin changes, ulcer)?
criteria.evidence_hint: 'CEAP', 'C2'...'C6' in assessment; or findings that define a class (varicose veins = C2, edema = C3, pigmentation/eczema = C4a, healed ulcer = C5, active ulcer = C6).

criteria.text: The varicosities are at least 3 millimeters in size
criteria.question: Are the varicosities documented as at least 3 mm in diameter?
criteria.evidence_hint: Vein diameter on duplex or exam: 'GSV 6.2 mm', 'varicosities up to 5 mm'.

criteria.question: Is there a venous stasis ulcer?
Is there documented recurrent superficial thrombophlebitis?

criteria.text: Hemorrhage or recurrent bleeding episodes from a ruptured superficial varicosity
criteria.question: Has a superficial varicosity ruptured and bled?

criteria.text: Persistent pain, swelling, itching, burning, or other symptoms are associated with saphenous reflux
criteria.question: Are there persistent symptoms (pain, swelling, itching, burning, heaviness, cramping) attributed to venous reflux?

criteria.text: The symptoms significantly interfere with activities of daily living
criteria.question: Do the documented symptoms significantly interfere with the patient's daily activities, work, or function?
criteria.evidence_hint: Limits standing/walking, missed work, stopped activities, sick days.

criteria.text: Conservative management including compression therapy for at least 3 months has not improved the symptoms
criteria.question: Has conservative management including compression stockings been tried for at least 3 months without symptom improvement?
criteria.evidence_hint: Compression stockings, 20-30 mmHg, start date and follow-up date, 'no improvement', 'symptoms persist'. Needs a duration, from dates or a stated number of months.

criteria.text: There is demonstrated accessory saphenous reflux
criteria.question: Does imaging demonstrate reflux in an accessory saphenous vein?

criteria.text: Incompetence of the accessory saphenous vein is isolated, or the great or small saphenous veins had been previously eliminated (at least 3 months)
criteria.question: Is the accessory saphenous incompetence isolated, or were the great/small saphenous veins treated at least 3 months ago?

criteria.text: Performed either at the same time or following prior treatment (surgical, radiofrequency, or laser) of the saphenous veins
criteria.question: Is the saphenous vein being treated concurrently, or was it previously treated by surgery, radiofrequency or laser?
Does imaging demonstrate reflux in a perforator vein?

criteria.text: The superficial saphenous veins (great, small, or accessory saphenous and symptomatic varicose tributaries) have been previously eliminated
criteria.question: Have the superficial saphenous veins and symptomatic tributaries already been treated?

criteria.text: Ulcers have not resolved following combined superficial vein treatment and compression therapy for at least 3 months
criteria.question: Have leg ulcers persisted for at least 3 months despite superficial vein treatment plus compression?

criteria.text: The venous insufficiency is secondary to deep venous thromboembolism
criteria.question: Is the venous insufficiency caused by prior deep vein thrombosis?
criteria.evidence_hint: History of DVT, post-thrombotic syndrome; or 'no history of DVT'.

scenarios.name: Symptomatic Varicose Tributaries
notes: Ultrasound guidance for sclerotherapy of tributaries does not meet medical necessity.

scenarios.name: Perforator Veins (leg ulcers with chronic venous insufficiency)

children.label: Not secondary to deep venous thromboembolism

notes: Ligation or ablation of perforator veins performed concurrently with superficial venous surgery does not meet medical necessity.
Treatment of telangiectasia (spider veins, angiomata, hemangiomata) is cosmetic and does not meet medical necessity (CPT 36468 non-covered).
Mechanochemical ablation (36473/36474), cryoablation, CHIVA, and 0524T are investigational.
Medicare Advantage products follow LCD L38720 / Article A58250 (FCSO), not this guideline.
